name: Daxos
description: Daxos is a servant of Heliod from Theros, remembered by Elspeth as her lost love and an old friend.

bio.text: He serves Heliod and is forced to carry out Heliod's will.
When Elspeth fell to Theros in a vision, Daxos's voice welcomed her as she saw Meletis in ruins.

bio.text: Elspeth treats him as an old friend she cannot forget.
Norn tempted her with a vision of unity with friends such as Ajani and Daxos, but she denied they were alike.

timeline.quote: "So you've not forgotten me, even with the new station,"

timeline.summary: Elspeth sees Ajani in Heliod's temple, converting gods and forcing a priestess to drink Phyrexian oil.
timeline.quote: He's already changed three of them.

citation.work: March of the Machine | Episode 6: The Last to Leave

timeline.summary: Elspeth weighs saving Theros against the larger war, and concludes the choice is not meant to be about her own wants.
timeline.quote: But this isn't meant to be about her own wants and needs.

citation.work: March of the Machine | Episode 6: The Last to Leave

timeline.summary: Elspeth is tempted by Norn's vision of unity with friends such as Ajani and Daxos, but denies they are alike.
timeline.quote: And though she is loath to admit it, there is truth to what Norn is saying.

citation.work: March of the Machine | Episode 7: Divine Intervention
citation.text: "March of the Machine | Episode 7: Divine Intervention" by K. Arsenault Rivera. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Mar 2023.

timeline.summary: Cymede offers herself to Keranos, who turns the Deyda River into an elemental that consumes the minotaurs; she ascends to Nyx.
timeline.quote: Cymede was claimed by Keranos as she transformed into a pillar of fire and crimson light and ascended into Nyx

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Erebos sends Athreos to take Daxos to the Underworld; despite Karametra's efforts Athreos seizes the boy, and Lidia offers herself in his place and is taken instead.
timeline.quote: Lidia offered herself in her son's place and was taken to the Underworld instead.

citation.text: "Athreos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lidia takes Daxos to Athreos; he speaks and is revealed to be an oracle; Erebos sends Athreos to claim him.
timeline.quote: Athreos was sent to claim the child

citation.text: "Daxos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lidia trades herself for her son and Karametra's emissary takes Daxos to safety.
timeline.quote: Lidia traded herself for her son

citation.text: "Daxos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth, helped by Daxos, slays Polukranos, becoming Heliod's champion.
timeline.quote: Elspeth engaged the hydra with the help of Daxos and succeeded where many had failed, slaying it

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Godsend". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Daxos travel to Akros, where Xenagos tells her how to destroy the army by raising the river.
timeline.quote: they raised the river that ran through Akros and swept the army away

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Daxos and Elspeth realize their feelings after the victory celebration.
timeline.quote: Daxos and Elspeth finally realized their feelings for each other

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos controls Elspeth, who kills Daxos while lashing out at the Phyrexian Obliterator in her memory.
timeline.quote: only realizing too late that she had just killed Daxos

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Daxos is freed from the Underworld as one of the Returned, searching for Elspeth.
timeline.quote: Daxos was freed from the Underworld in a cruel bargain with Erebos

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Daxos the Returned". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elevated to demigod, Daxos is reformed by Heliod to destroy signs of other divinities in Meletis.
timeline.quote: He was reformed by Heliod with the task of destroying every sign of other divinities in Meletis

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Demigod". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Daxos fights in defense of Theros during the New Phyrexian Invasion.
timeline.quote: Daxos fought in defense of Theros during the New Phyrexian Invasion

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Demigod". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth slays the hydra Polukranos and becomes Heliod's champion.
timeline.quote: Elspeth engaged the hydra with the help of Daxos and succeeded where so many had failed, slaying it.

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Daxos realize their feelings after Akros is saved.
timeline.quote: Daxos and Elspeth finally realize their feelings for each other.

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "The Great Revel". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos controls Elspeth; she kills the Obliterator in her memory and realizes she has killed Daxos.
timeline.quote: only realizing too late that she had just killed Daxos

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "The Great Revel". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Erebos sends Athreos to fetch Daxos for his oracular gift; Lidia takes her son's place and is brought to the Underworld.
timeline.quote: thus she was brought to the Underworld while Daxos was left alone in the Mortal Realm.

citation.text: "Erebos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After Elspeth slays Xenagos, Heliod has Daxos remove traces of other gods from Meletis; the gods go to war, rifts open to the Underworld, and Erebos neglects the souls under his charge out of hatred of Heliod.
timeline.quote: He hated Heliod most of all, and in his rage, he neglected to keep a tight grip on the souls under his purview.

citation.text: "Erebos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod resurrects Daxos as a demigod at great cost while seeking to become sole god.
timeline.quote: Heliod sought to become the sole god of the pantheon.

citation.text: "Heliod", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod makes the oracle Daxos his champion and orders him to remove the other gods from Meletis; the gods go to war.
timeline.quote: he pulled the soul of the oracle Daxos and transformed him into his champion in the mortal realm

citation.text: "Meletis", section "Beyond Death". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: When Heliod has Daxos purge Meletis of other gods' influence, Purphoros and the others summon champions from the Underworld, Purphoros choosing Anax.
timeline.quote: Purphoros’s champion was Anax , former king of Akros .

citation.text: "Purphoros", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth offers her life for Daxos; Erebos accepts and Heliod fatally wounds his former champion.
timeline.quote: Elspeth offered her life in trade for her lover Daxos .

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod makes Daxos his champion to purge the other gods from Meletis, starting a war of the gods and opening rifts to the Underworld.
timeline.quote: the gods were at war

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "War of the gods". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth planeswalks away with Calix, whose spark ignites.
timeline.quote: Elspeth planeswalked away, with Calix, whose spark ignited in the meantime, following her.

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "War of the gods". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod transforms Daxos into his Champion and orders him to remove all trace of the other gods from Meletis.
timeline.quote: Daxos was instructed to remove all trace of the other gods from the great city of Meletis

citation.text: "War of the Gods", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After a brief reunion with Daxos Elspeth planeswalks away, and Calix sparks and planeswalks after her.
timeline.quote: a spark flared inside him, and he planeswalked after her

citation.text: "War of the Gods", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After a Great Revel following the siege of Akros, Xenagos ascended to godhood as god of revels, and Elspeth was scapegoated for Daxos's death and exiled.
timeline.quote: Xenagos held the position of the god of the revels, furthering the chaos and distrust of the established pantheon.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Return to Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.
